claims.text: What the strip looks like At magnesium 6 to 12 mg/dL the ECG shows a long PR interval, a wide QRS and taller T waves.
claims.quote: At serum magnesium concentrations of 6 to 12 mg/dL (2.5 to 5 mmol/L), the ECG shows prolongation of the PR interval, widening of the QRS complex, and increased T-wave amplitude.

claims.text: T wave (6 to 12 mg/dL): increased amplitude
claims.quote: At serum magnesium concentrations of 6 to 12 mg/dL (2.5 to 5 mmol/L), the ECG shows prolongation of the PR interval, widening of the QRS complex, and increased T-wave amplitude.

claims.text: Magnesium > 15 mg/dL: cardiac arrest may occur
claims.quote: Cardiac arrest may occur when blood magnesium concentration is > 15 mg/dL (6.0 to 7.5 mmol/L).

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Symptomatic hypermagnesemia is fairly uncommon
Most common: kidney failure after taking magnesium-containing medications (antacids, purgatives); it may also occur with diabetic ketoacidosis, hypothyroidism, and hyperparathyroidism
claims.quote: It occurs most commonly in patients with kidney failure after ingestion of magnesium-containing medications, such as antacids or purgatives. Hypermagnesemia may also occur in patients with diabetic ketoacidosis, hypothyroidism, and hyperparathyroidism.

claims.text: Even asymptomatic hypermagnesemia is rare with normal kidney function
claims.quote: Even asymptomatic hypermagnesemia is rare in patients with normal kidney function.

claims.text: Symptoms Hyporeflexia, hypotension, respiratory depression, and cardiac arrest
claims.quote: Symptoms and signs include hyporeflexia, hypotension, respiratory depression, and cardiac arrest.

claims.text: Deep tendon reflexes disappear as magnesium approaches 12 mg/dL; hypotension, respiratory depression and narcosis develop as it rises
claims.quote: Deep tendon reflexes disappear as the serum magnesium concentration approaches 12 mg/dL (5.0 mmol/L); hypotension, respiratory depression, and narcosis develop with increasing hypermagnesemia.

claims.text: Treatment Severe toxicity (e.g., 12 mg/dL): circulatory and respiratory support plus 10% calcium gluconate 10 to 20 mL IV, which may temporarily reverse many of the changes, including respiratory depression
claims.quote: Treatment of severe magnesium toxicity (eg, 12 mg/dL [5.0 mmol/L]) consists of circulatory and respiratory support and administration of 10% calcium gluconate 10 to 20 mL IV. Calcium gluconate may temporarily reverse many of the magnesium-induced changes, including respiratory depression.

claims.text: IV furosemide can increase magnesium excretion when kidney function is adequate; maintain volume status
claims.quote: Administration of IV furosemide can increase magnesium excretion when kidney function is adequate; volume status should be maintained.

claims.text: Hemodialysis may be valuable in severe hypermagnesemia (about 70% of blood magnesium is not protein-bound and is removable)
claims.quote: Hemodialysis may be valuable in severe hypermagnesemia, because a relatively large fraction (approximately 70%) of magnesium in the blood is not protein-bound and thus is removable with hemodialysis.
